key_idea: With clamping at zero, the final stench of a walk equals max(0, largest suffix sum), so binary search the answer X and ask, walking backwards from n, whether node 1 is reachable while the running sum never exceeds X; negative cycles reachable under that budget make everything behind them reachable.
sketch: Reverse all edges and run Bellman-Ford from n where a relaxation is allowed only if the new distance is <= X. If after n rounds some edge can still relax, its head lies behind a negative cycle that is feasible under the budget (removing a non-negative cycle never hurts feasibility), so mark those nodes as -infinity and propagate -infinity along reversed edges without any budget test. X is feasible iff node 1 is reached; binary search X in [0, 2e12]. Complexity O(n*m*log(2e12)) ~ 1.7e8. Pitfalls: plain Bellman-Ford on the clamped recurrence converges only pseudo-polynomially (sample 2 needs ~500 laps of the cycle), a negative cycle does not automatically give 0 at every node, and sums need 64 bits. Stress-tested against value iteration on small graphs.
